##Data cleaning and adjusting
```{r}
##Group Blood pressure Edit
#Change blood pressure
Systolic <- list()
for (value in data$Blood.Pressure) {
  systolic_pressure <- strsplit(value, "/")[[1]][1] #Create new element
  Systolic[[length(Systolic) + 1]] <- systolic_pressure
}

#Two parts of the blood pressure, diastole is the lower
Diastolic <- list()
for (value in data$Blood.Pressure) {
  diastolic_pressure <- strsplit(value, "/")[[1]][2] #Create new element
  Diastolic[[length(Diastolic) + 1]] <- diastolic_pressure
}
Systolic <- as.integer(Systolic)
Diastolic <- as.integer(Diastolic)

data$Systolic <- Systolic
data$Diastolic <- Diastolic

#Group blood pressure
#Reference from: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/high-blood-pressure/in-depth/blood-pressure/art-20050982
data$BP <- ifelse(data$Diastolic<80 & data$Systolic<120, "Normal", 
                  ifelse(data$Diastolic<80 & (120 <= data$Systolic | data$Systolic <= 129), "Elevated",
                         ifelse((80 <= data$Diastolic | data$Diastolic <= 89) & (130 <= data$Systolic | data$Systolic <= 139), "High", "Low")))

#Group Sleep quality 
data$Sleep.Quality.Group <- ifelse(1<=data$Quality.of.Sleep & data$Quality.of.Sleep<=4, "Low Quality",
                             ifelse(5<=data$Quality.of.Sleep & data$Quality.of.Sleep<=7, "Medium Quality", "High Quality"))

```


##Creation of Descriptive Statistics Tables
```{r}
#Function for continuous data
continuous_summary <- function(data, vars) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {
    x <- data[[v]]
    data.frame(
      Variable = v,
      Mean = round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      SD = round(sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      Median = round(median(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      Min = round(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      Max = round(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    )
  }))
}
#Continuous Data variables
continuous_vars <- c(
  "Age",
  "Sleep.Duration",
  "Quality.of.Sleep",
  "Physical.Activity.Level",
  "Stress.Level",
  "Heart.Rate",
  "Daily.Steps"
)
continuous_table <- continuous_summary(data, continuous_vars)

#Function for categorical data
categorical_summary <- function(data, vars) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {
    counts <- table(data[[v]])
    percents <- prop.table(counts) * 100
    data.frame(
      Variable = v,
      Category = names(counts),
      Count = as.vector(counts),
      `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", counts, percents)
    )
  }))
}

#Categorical variables
categorical_vars <- c(
  "Gender",
  "BP",
  "Occupation",
  "Sleep.Disorder"
)
categorical_table <- categorical_summary(data, categorical_vars)

```

###Decision tree modeling
```{r}
#The dplyr package allows removing columns from the file.
df <- data %>% select(-BMI.Category, -Blood.Pressure, -Person.ID,
                      -Systolic, -Diastolic, -Quality.of.Sleep,
                      -Daily.Steps)

#All character columns are converted to factor columns
#Required input for confusion matrix generation
df[sapply(df, is.character)] <- lapply(df[sapply(df, is.character)], 
                                       as.factor)
```

```{r}
#Random seperation of the dataset into training and testing
train_index <- createDataPartition(df$Sleep.Disorder, p=0.8, list=FALSE)
train_data <- df[train_index, ]
test_data <- df[-train_index,]

#Creation of the machine learning model
tree_model <- rpart(Sleep.Disorder ~ .,
                    data = train_data,
                    method = "class",
                    control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 3, cp=0.001))

#Plotting the model via rpart.plot module
rpart.plot(tree_model, box.palette = "Purples", nn = TRUE)

#Choose levels with hyperparameter "maxdepth", minimum number of examples in
# a node to perform a split - "minsplit", minimum number of examples in a 
# terminal node - "minbucket", split must increase performance - "cp"
```
```{r}
#Creation of confusion matrix
predictions <- predict(tree_model, test_data, type = "class")
#Typecasting predictions into factor and use of test_data's variable of interest
#as it is the same length, do not use the dataframes variable
confusionMatrix(as.factor(predictions), test_data$Sleep.Disorder)

#str(predictions)
#str(df$Sleep.Disorder)

#length(predictions)
#length(test_data$Sleep.Disorder)
```
```{r}
#Random seperation of the dataset into training and testing
train_index <- createDataPartition(df$Sleep.Quality, p=0.8, list=FALSE)
train_data <- df[train_index, ]
test_data <- df[-train_index,]

#Creation of the machine learning model
tree_model <- rpart(Sleep.Quality.Group ~ .,
                    data = train_data,
                    method = "class",
                    control = rpart.control(minsplit = 10, cp = 0.01))

#Plotting the model via rpart.plot module
rpart.plot(tree_model, box.palette = "Purples", nn = TRUE, main = "Sleep Quality Decision Tree")
```

```{r}
#Creation of confusion matrix
predictions <- predict(tree_model, test_data, type = "class")
#Typecasting predictions into factor and use of test_data's variable of interest
#as it is the same length, do not use the dataframes variable
confusionMatrix(as.factor(predictions), test_data$Sleep.Quality)
```

```{r}
#The data without the labels is instantiated
unlabeled_df <- df %>% select(-Sleep.Disorder, -Sleep.Quality.Group)

#All features need to be numeric for scaling
#Turn Female -> 1, Male -> 2
#Turn Elevated -> 1, High -> 2, Normal -> 3
unlabeled_df[] <- lapply(unlabeled_df, as.numeric)
unlabeled_df_1 <- unlabeled_df
#glimpse(unlabeled_df)

#Scaling the data, distance matrix needs to be unweighted, balances the dataset
#Makes all features important, no matter how big the scale is
unlabeled_df_scale <- scale(unlabeled_df)

#Apply the scale to the data set, method is default Euclidean
unlabeled_df <- dist(unlabeled_df_scale)

#Elbow method, within sum squares -> wss
#Gives us a plot that tells us the optimal number of clusters that we should begin with
fviz_nbclust(unlabeled_df_scale, kmeans, method = "wss") + 
  labs(subtitle = "Elbow method")
```

###Non-Parametric Tests
```{r}
#Tests
#Spearman tests for continuous data. It shows association between sleep quality and variable.
age <- cor.test(data2$Age, data2$Quality.of.Sleep, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

sleep_hours <- cor.test(data2$Sleep.Duration, data2$Quality.of.Sleep, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

activity_level <- cor.test(data2$Physical.Activity.Level, data2$Quality.of.Sleep, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

stress_level <- cor.test(data2$Stress.Level, data2$Quality.of.Sleep, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

heart_rate <- cor.test(data2$Heart.Rate, data2$Quality.of.Sleep, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

daily_steps <- cor.test(data2$Daily.Steps, data2$Quality.of.Sleep, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

#Mann-Whitney tests for binary categorical data. It shows how sleep quality differs between female and male
gender <- wilcox.test(Quality.of.Sleep ~ Gender, data = data2)


#Kruskal-Wallis tests for ordinal data. It also shows how sleep quality differs between each subgroup of these variables.

bp_test <- kruskal.test(Quality.of.Sleep ~ BP, data = data2)

occupation_group <- kruskal.test(Quality.of.Sleep ~ OccupationGroup, data = data2)

sleep_disorder <- kruskal.test(Quality.of.Sleep ~Sleep.Disorder, data = data2)

occupation <- kruskal.test(Quality.of.Sleep ~Occupation, data = data2)

```

##Obtain Effect sizes for Mann-W and KW
```{r}
#Mann-Whitney effect size calculation
rank_biserial(Quality.of.Sleep ~ Gender, data = data2)
gender_es <- rank_biserial(Quality.of.Sleep ~ Gender, data = data2)


#Kruskal-Wallis effect size calculation
kruskal_effsize(data2, Quality.of.Sleep ~ BP)
bp_es <- kruskal_effsize(data2, Quality.of.Sleep ~ BP)
occupation_es <- kruskal_effsize(data2, Quality.of.Sleep ~ Occupation)
sleepdisorder_es <- kruskal_effsize(data2, Quality.of.Sleep ~ Sleep.Disorder)


#Extract effect size Mann-W
gender_effect <- gender_es$r_rank_biserial

#Extract effect size KW
bp_effect <- bp_es$effsize
occupation_effect <- occupation_es$effsize
sleepdisorder_effect <- sleepdisorder_es$effsize

#Build table with all effect sizes from the 3 tests
results <- data.frame(
  Variable = c(
    "Age",
    "Sleep Duration (Hours)",
    "Physical Activity (Minutes/Day)",
    "Stress Level",
    "Heart Rate",
    "Daily Steps",
    "Gender",
    "Blood Pressure",
    "Sleep Disorder",
    "Occupation"
  ),
  Test = c(
    rep("Spearman", 6),
    rep("Mann-Whitney U", 1),
    rep("Kruskal-Wallis", 3)
  ),
  Effect_Size = c(
    #Spearman rho
    age$estimate,
    sleep_hours$estimate,
    activity_level$estimate,
    stress_level$estimate,
    heart_rate$estimate,
    daily_steps$estimate,
    #Mann-Whitney rank biserial
    gender_effect,
    #Kruskal-Wallis epsilon squared
    bp_effect,
    sleepdisorder_effect,
    occupation_effect
  ),
  Effect_Type = c(
    rep("Spearman rho", 6),
    rep("Rank-biserial correlation", 1),
    rep("Epsilon squared", 3)
  ),
  P_value = c(
    #Spearman p-values
    age$p.value,
    sleep_hours$p.value,
    activity_level$p.value,
    stress_level$p.value,
    heart_rate$p.value,
    daily_steps$p.value,
    #Mann-Whitney p-values
    gender$p.value,
    #Kruskal-Wallis p-values
    bp_test$p.value,
    sleep_disorder$p.value,
    occupation$p.value
  )
)

#Formatting table
results <- results %>%
  mutate(Effect_Size = round(as.numeric(Effect_Size), 3),
         P_value = signif(P_value, 3),
         neg_log10_p = round(-log10(P_value), 2))

#Make results significant if p-value is lower than 0.01
results$Significant <- ifelse(results$P_value < 0.01, "Yes", "No")

#Save table
write.csv(results, "all_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

##Plot effect sizes
```{r}
#Function for plotting Spearman
effect_plot <- function(data, test_name, title, y_label) {
  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(Test == test_name) %>%
    mutate(Variable = reorder(Variable, Effect_Size),
           Label_Position = ifelse(abs(Effect_Size) < 0.15,
                                   Effect_Size + ifelse(Effect_Size > 0, 0.05, -0.05),
                                   Effect_Size - ifelse(Effect_Size > 0, 0.05, -0.05)))
  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(x = Variable, y = Effect_Size, fill = Effect_Size > 0)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(y = Label_Position, label = round(Effect_Size, 2)), color = ifelse(abs(plot_data$Effect_Size) < 0.15, "black", "white"),
              fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    coord_flip() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-1, 1, 0.2)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#720e9e", "#FF69B4"), guide = "none") +
    labs(title = title,x = "", y = y_label) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

effect_plot(results,
  "Spearman",
  "Spearman Correlation with Sleep Quality",
  expression(rho)
)

#KW
kruskal_effect_plot <- function(data, title) {
  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(Test == "Kruskal-Wallis") %>%
    mutate(Variable = reorder(Variable, Effect_Size), Label_Position = ifelse(Effect_Size < 0.05, Effect_Size + 0.03, Effect_Size - 0.03))
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Variable, y = Effect_Size, fill = Effect_Size)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(y = Label_Position, label = round(Effect_Size, 2)), color = ifelse(abs(plot_data$Effect_Size) < 0.05, "black", "white"), 
              fontface= "bold", size = 4) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#E8D5F5", high = "#720e9e", guide = "none") +
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = expression(epsilon^2)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 18), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
kruskal_effect_plot(results, "Kruskal–Wallis Effect Size on Sleep Quality")
```

The correlation plot includes only numeric variables. Variables such as occupation, BMI category, sleep disorder and blood-pressure category are factors and should not be converted into arbitrary numeric codes for Pearson correlation.

# Training and test split
```{r}
set.seed(123)

train_index <- createDataPartition(
  df_linear$BP,
  p = 0.80,
  list = FALSE
)

train_df <- df_linear[train_index, ]
test_df  <- df_linear[-train_index, ]

cat("Training observations:", nrow(train_df), "\n")
cat("Test observations:", nrow(test_df), "\n")
```

# Full multiple linear regression model
```{r}
# The full model contains all available predictors
full_model <- lm(
  Quality.of.Sleep ~ .,
  data = train_df)
summary(full_model)
```

# Backward model selection using BIC
```{r}
# BIC applies a stronger complexity penalty than AIC
# BIC uses k = log(n), where n is the number of training observations

backward_BIC <- step(
  full_model,
  direction = "backward",
  k = log(nrow(train_df)),
  trace = FALSE
)

formula(backward_BIC)
summary(backward_BIC)
```

# Selected and removed predictors
```{r}
full_predictors <- attr(
  terms(full_model),
  "term.labels"
)

selected_predictors <- attr(
  terms(backward_BIC),
  "term.labels"
)

removed_predictors <- setdiff(
  full_predictors,
  selected_predictors
)

cat("Selected predictors:\n")
print(selected_predictors)

cat("\nRemoved predictors:\n")
print(removed_predictors)
```

# Training-model comparison
```{r}
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Full Model", "Backward BIC"),
  BIC = c(
    BIC(full_model),
    BIC(backward_BIC)
  ),
  Features = c(
    length(attr(terms(full_model), "term.labels")),
    length(attr(terms(backward_BIC), "term.labels"))
  ),
  Adj_R2 = c(
    summary(full_model)$adj.r.squared,
    summary(backward_BIC)$adj.r.squared
  )
)

ggplot(
  model_comparison,
  aes(
    x = Model,
    y = BIC,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.45) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0(
        Features, " features\n",
        "Adj. R² = ", round(Adj_R2, 3)
      )
    ),
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("#7A0177", "#DD3497")
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Model Comparison Using BIC",
    x = NULL,
    y = "BIC"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5,
      size = 13
    ),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )
```

# Test-set predictions
```{r}
pred_full <- predict(
  full_model,
  newdata = test_df)

pred_BIC <- predict(
  backward_BIC,
  newdata = test_df)
```

# Test-set evaluation

```{r}
evaluate_model <- function(actual, predicted) {
  residuals <- actual - predicted
  RSS <- sum(residuals^2)
  MSE <- mean(residuals^2)
  R2 <- 1 -
    sum((actual - predicted)^2) /
    sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
  return(
    c(
      RSS = RSS,
      MSE = MSE,
      R2 = R2))}
```

```{r}
full_test_results <- evaluate_model(
  actual = test_df$Quality.of.Sleep,
  predicted = pred_full)

BIC_test_results <- evaluate_model(
  actual = test_df$Quality.of.Sleep,
  predicted = pred_BIC)

test_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Full model",
    "Backward BIC model"),

  RSS = c(
    full_test_results["RSS"],
    BIC_test_results["RSS"]),

  MSE = c(
    full_test_results["MSE"],
    BIC_test_results["MSE"]),

  Test_R2 = c(
    full_test_results["R2"],
    BIC_test_results["R2"]))

test_comparison %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric),
      ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Test Performance of the Full and BIC-Selected Models") %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c(
      "striped",
      "hover",
      "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE)
```

# Actual and predicted values
```{r}
prediction_results <- data.frame(
  Actual = test_df$Quality.of.Sleep,
  Predicted = as.numeric(pred_BIC),
  Residual = test_df$Quality.of.Sleep -
    as.numeric(pred_BIC))

ggplot(
  prediction_results,
  aes(
    x = Actual,
    y = Predicted
  )) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +

  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Multicollinearity
```{r}
# Generalized VIF is returned because the model contains factor variables
vif_results <- car::vif(backward_BIC)

if (is.matrix(vif_results)) {

  # Keep only the adjusted GVIF column
  vif_table <- data.frame(
    Predictor = rownames(vif_results),
    Adjusted_GVIF = vif_results[, "GVIF^(1/(2*Df))"],
    row.names = NULL
  )

  vif_table %>%
    mutate(
      Adjusted_GVIF = round(Adjusted_GVIF, 3)
    ) %>%
    kable(
      col.names = c(
        "Predictor",
        "Adjusted GVIF"
      ),
      caption = "Adjusted Generalized Variance Inflation Factors"
    ) %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c(
        "striped",
        "hover",
        "condensed"
      ),
      full_width = FALSE)
} else {

  # This section is used if the model contains only one-degree-of-freedom predictors
  vif_table <- data.frame(
    Predictor = names(vif_results),
    VIF = as.numeric(vif_results))

  vif_table %>%
    mutate(
      VIF = round(VIF, 3)) %>%
    kable(
      caption = "Variance Inflation Factors") %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c(
        "striped",
        "hover",
        "condensed"),
      full_width = FALSE)}
```

Because the model contains categorical predictors with multiple levels, the adjusted measure \(GVIF^{1/(2\times Df)}\) was interpreted. All adjusted GVIF values were below 5, indicating that multicollinearity was not a major concern in the final model.
